system_description.narrative_title: AI buildout strains markets, security, and financing
system_description.narrative_summary: This window centers on a single systemic story: the rapid, capital‑intensive AI buildout (neoclouds, chips, and model training) is colliding with investor risk aversion, insurance/credit stresses, and a surge in AI‑related cybersecurity flaws. As an open system, capital, data, talent, exploits, and regulatory signals flow between tech firms, infrastructure providers, financiers/insurers, researchers, and states, generating reinforcing feedbacks (market selloffs → funding squeezes → concentrated counterparty risk) and balancing responses (patching, regulation, insurance, and spending cuts). The result is market volatility, funding bottlenecks for AI infrastructure, and urgent policy/security actions.
system_description.scope: Global AI infrastructure buildout and its proximate effects: neocloud/data centers, chipmakers, major AI developers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Nvidia), corporate AI spending decisions, capital and insurance markets (banks, hedge funds, default insurance), cybersecurity vulnerabilities and incident responses, and near‑term regulatory/policy reactions.
system_description.super_system: Global financial system and digital‑technology ecosystem (macroeconomy, capital markets, and geopolitics of tech competition).
adjacent_subsystems: Cybersecurity ecosystem (vulnerability researchers, incident response, national CERTs)
Capital markets & insurance (credit markets, insurers, CDS/DI markets, hedge funds)
Semiconductor & data center supply chain (chipmakers, equipment, colo/neocloud operators)
Regulatory & policy apparatus (financial regulators, national security/cyber policy, standards bodies)
evidence_headlines: America’s $10tn AI infrastructure boom is starting to fray
AI debt worries spark surge in default insurance trading
CoreWeave set off a wave of anxiety — but Wall Street’s dire prognosis is premature
AI-discovered bugs may soon trigger fresh disruptions, cyber experts say
S&P 500, Nasdaq end sharply lower as revived AI doubts ignite tech selloff

variables.name: Compute infrastructure capacity
variables.description: The aggregate available compute resources for AI training and inference (e.g., total GPU/accelerator cycles and datacenter provisioning).

variables.name: Compute demand growth rate
variables.description: The rate of change in demand for compute resources driven by model scale, frequency of training, and inference workloads.

variables.name: Capital availability for AI buildout
variables.description: The supply of investable finance available for AI infrastructure, model development, and related projects across public and private markets.

variables.name: Infrastructure financing cost
variables.description: The effective cost of raising capital for AI infrastructure, including interest spreads, credit premia, and lending terms.

variables.name: Investor risk aversion level
variables.description: The prevailing appetite or reluctance of investors to fund speculative or capital‑intensive AI projects, as reflected in portfolio allocations and flows.

variables.name: Insurance capacity for AI risks
variables.description: The availability and depth of insurance coverage and underwriting willingness for AI‑specific operational, cyber and liability risks.

variables.name: Cyber vulnerability prevalence
variables.description: The aggregate prevalence and severity of software and system vulnerabilities that can be exploited in AI and adjacent infrastructure.

variables.name: Cyber exploit incident rate
variables.description: The frequency at which cyber exploits, intrusions, or large‑scale misuse events occur against AI systems and connected infrastructure.

variables.name: Patching and mitigation speed
variables.description: The speed and throughput at which vulnerabilities are detected, patched, and mitigations deployed across systems and ecosystems.

variables.name: Counterparty concentration risk
variables.description: The degree to which critical AI infrastructure, financing, or services are concentrated among a small set of counterparties, increasing systemic exposure.

variables.name: Corporate AI spending rate
variables.description: The pace at which corporations commit and disburse capital to AI projects, infrastructure, and procurement over time.

variables.name: Model training cost per unit
variables.description: The marginal cost to train or fine‑tune a unit of model capacity (e.g., per trillion FLOPs or per training run), including compute, energy, and storage.

variables.name: Specialist talent supply
variables.description: The available pool of skilled personnel for AI engineering, operations, security, and research relative to demand.

variables.name: Regulatory scrutiny intensity
variables.description: The level and vigor of regulatory examination, enforcement, and policy activity focused on AI systems, infrastructure, and associated risks.

variables.name: Market volatility level
variables.description: The magnitude of price and liquidity fluctuations in financial markets that affect valuation and funding for AI and tech assets.

variables.name: Training data availability
variables.description: The volume, diversity, and accessibility of data suitable for training and validating AI models across domains.

catalysts.title: Neocloud financing squeeze
catalysts.description: Pressure on specialist "neocloud" providers to refinance or reduce capacity as debt and short-selling hits valuations and lenders tighten terms.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'neoclouds take market hit', 'Nvidia's role as AI financier faces first big test', 'Short sellers make $6 billion'.

catalysts.title: AI insurance market tightens
catalysts.description: Underwriters restrict AI coverage and raise premiums as losses, exposures and demand for specialized policies surge.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AI Runs Into Its Next Big Obstacle: Insurance', 'CoreWeave targets ‘unlimited’ insurance money', 'default insurance trading surge'.

catalysts.title: Global PHP-flaw exploit wave
catalysts.description: Ongoing exploitation and rapid patching of critical PHP vulnerabilities will drive high incident volumes and security actions across the internet.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AI's "Black October": Critical PHP flaws', 'websites taken offline', 'hacking attempts surge', 'AI-discovered bugs may soon trigger fresh disruptions.'

catalysts.title: Banks restrict third‑party AI agent access
catalysts.description: Major banks block or curtail third‑party AI agents' access to customer accounts, limiting data flows and deployment models for agentified services.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US banks are blocking third-party AI agents access to customer accounts', 'Citi becomes latest US bank to restrict AI agents.'

catalysts.title: National cyber simulations and AI security funding
catalysts.description: Planned government exercises and funding (e.g., Japan simulations, UK $800M) will accelerate defensive programs and procurement.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Japan to simulate cyberattacks', 'UK government sets out $800 million of AI security funding.'

catalysts.title: Market reassessment of AI valuations and funding
catalysts.description: A broad re-pricing of AI assets and portfolios as investors digest high spending, credit signals and security risks, affecting funding and volatility.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AI funding fears rattle Wall Street', 'Calpers retreats', 'Meta credit risk indicator hits record high', 'stock selloff continues.'

catalysts.title: Shift to offline/no‑internet frontier training
catalysts.description: Industry moves to mandate or prefer offline isolated training for frontier models, concentrating secure compute and altering demand patterns.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'OpenAI mandates offline training for frontier models', 'OpenAI resumes frontier AI training with enhanced security, no internet access.'

catalysts.title: Large AI fundraises and IPO activity
catalysts.description: Outsize private raises and pending IPOs (and pulled listings) will reallocate capital and signal risk appetite across the sector.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'DeepSeek Raises $15 Billion', 'Anthropic S-1 shows red-hot growth', 'Solidigm pulls IPO', 'AI funding fears rattle Wall Street.'
